title: Cabinet Refinishing in Micanopy, FL | Older Kitchens
description: Cabinet refinishing in Micanopy, FL for older kitchens and built-ins. Degrease, repair, bond-prime, and spray waterborne urethane enamel. Free estimates.
heroIntro: Older kitchens and built-ins often have solid wood worth keeping. We repair, prime, and refinish them in a hard enamel so they look fresh without losing their character.

questions: Can you paint old wood cabinets and built-ins?
How do you keep painted cabinets from peeling in humid weather?
Should I refinish or replace my kitchen cabinets?

sections.h2: Kitchens and built-ins in older Micanopy homes
body: Pre-war houses often have cabinetry with history: solid wood boxes, built-in hutches, pantry cupboards, or bathroom vanities that have been painted more than once. Replacing them can erase part of what makes the house special, and new boxes rarely fit odd old walls the same way. Cabinet refinishing in Micanopy, FL keeps what is good and fixes what is not.
Newer homes around town bring a different starting point: factory-finished oak or maple that is sound but dated. Both can be refinished; the prep just differs.

Cabinets in older homes usually need some carpentry attention before finishing. We tighten loose hinges and joints, fill gouges and old hardware holes, and sand away drips and buildup from past paint jobs so the new coat goes on flat. Every surface is degreased, because cooking film is the number one cause of cabinet paint failure.

Then comes a bonding primer matched to the surface, whether bare wood, a factory finish, or old paint of unknown age. In a humid town with damp shaded houses, that bond is what keeps the finish from lifting at edges and corners.

Glass-front doors on hutches and upper cabinets are common in older kitchens. We mask the glass carefully and cut the muntins by hand, since overspray on old wavy glass is hard to remove cleanly. Original hardware can be cleaned and reinstalled if you want to keep it, or swapped for something new while the doors are off.

bullets: Two coats of waterborne urethane enamel, sprayed for a smooth surface
A harder, more cleanable finish than wall paint
Color matched from a chip, a cabinet door, or a leftover can
Full-size drawdowns so you can see the color in your kitchen's light
Doors and hardware labelled and returned to their original spots
body: Built-ins and hutches in living or dining rooms are handled the same way, with surrounding floors and walls protected.

Cabinet work takes several days because enamel needs time to level and harden between coats. You can stay in the house, and we keep the work contained. Pairing cabinets with walls and trim through interior painting in Micanopy finishes the room at once. Choosing a color for an older kitchen? Our color consultation helps.
For more reading, see refinish vs. replace cabinets and our main cabinet painting and refinishing page.

faqs.q: Can you paint built-in cabinets and hutches in an older home?
faqs.a: Yes. We repair, degrease, prime, and finish them in waterborne urethane enamel, the same system we use on kitchen cabinets.

faqs.q: Will humidity make painted cabinets peel?
faqs.a: Peeling usually comes from grease or poor adhesion, not humidity alone. Thorough degreasing and a bonding primer are what keep the finish attached.

faqs.q: Can you match the color of my existing trim?
faqs.a: Yes. We match from a chip, a door, or a leftover can and show a full-size drawdown before spraying.
